title: OffSec OSEP
summary: OffSec OSEP, the Experienced Penetration Tester certification, is an advanced hands-on credential for penetration testers who already hold a working certification and now need to operate against defended, modern networks. It sits above entry level and assumes you can already run a basic engagement. The exam is a long practical assessment in which you attack a simulated enterprise while a security operations centre watches, so stealth and defence evasion matter as much as exploitation. OffSec does not publish per domain weightings for this exam, so the chapter list below gives the official domain names without percentages. Passing proves to an employer that you can evade endpoint protection, bypass application controls, and move through Windows and Linux estates, and it leads to roles such as senior penetration tester, red team operator, and security consultant. The domain structure below follows the published objectives; check the vendor's current version before booking.

beginner.definition: OSEP is an advanced certification from OffSec for penetration testers who already have experience. A penetration tester is a security professional paid to attack a company's own systems with permission. OSEP focuses on attacking networks that have modern defences in place. OffSec calls the credential the Experienced Penetration Tester certification.
beginner.whyItMatters: Many networks now run endpoint protection and application controls that block simple attacks. This certification proves you can work around those defences. An employer sees that you can stay quiet during an assessment instead of being caught straight away. It is a strong step up from a first certification and supports red team roles. It also shows you can keep working when a target does not behave as expected.
howItWorks: Start only after you can complete a basic network penetration test without help.
Learn how defenders detect attackers. Study antimalware, logging, and monitoring so you know what noise you make.
Practise writing your own small tools in a scripting language so you are not limited to off the shelf programs.
Study defences such as application allow lists and how attackers get around them in a lab you own.
Build a home lab with Windows and Linux targets, and practise pivoting between networks.
The exam is a long practical assessment. You must compromise the environment while staying undetected, then submit a report.
beginner.example: Imagine you are asked to test a bank vault. This vault has cameras and a guard who reacts to any noise. A beginner walks in through the front door and is caught at once. An experienced tester studies the guard's routine, finds the blind spot, and only moves when the camera is turned away. OffSec OSEP tests the second approach. It does not ask whether you can get in, because you already can. It asks whether you can get in without being noticed.
takeaways: Do not start here. Pass an entry level certification and get real practice first.
Stealth is graded. A loud attack that works may still count as a failure.
OffSec does not publish domain weights for this exam, so plan study time by your own weak areas.

objectives: Write small custom tools in a scripting language to support an engagement
Evade antimalware and endpoint detection so your activity is not alerted on
Bypass application allow lists and other host controls on a Windows target
Move between network segments by using a compromised host as a pivot
Attack Active Directory environments and take control of the domain
Produce a professional assessment report that explains findings and business impact

chapters.title: Penetration testing with a focus on operational security
objectives: Plan an engagement so that each action supports a clear objective
Write custom tools when standard tools would be blocked or too noisy
Understand the logging and monitoring that defenders rely on
Keep your activity inside the rules of engagement agreed with the client

chapters.title: Defence evasion and breaking out of restricted environments
objectives: Bypass antimalware and endpoint detection using several different techniques
Defeat application allow list controls without disabling them
Execute code on a target while leaving as little trace as possible
Choose an evasion method that suits the target operating system and build

chapters.title: Network and cloud security and pivoting
objectives: Use a compromised host as a pivot to reach systems on another network
Build and manage tunnels that carry your traffic through segmented networks
Enumerate reachable services from a pivot and identify the next target
Recognise misconfigurations in cloud hosted services that enable access

chapters.title: Microsoft Windows and Active Directory attacks
objectives: Enumerate an Active Directory domain and map users, groups, and trusts
Use credential access techniques to obtain and reuse account secrets
Exploit common Active Directory misconfigurations to gain higher privileges
Escalate to domain administrator and demonstrate full control of the estate

chapters.title: Linux security and privilege escalation
objectives: Enumerate a Linux host for services, permissions, and scheduled tasks
Find and exploit a vulnerable network service on the host
Escalate from a low privileged account to root on the target
Maintain access to a Linux host without breaking the client's business

chapters.title: Web application attacks and reporting
objectives: Test a web application for common flaws and chain them into real access
Turn individual findings into a clear attack narrative for the client
Write a report that separates technical detail from business impact
